original_question: Let M be a smooth real hypersurface in C^n with defining function r. Let p0 be a point in M, and let U be a neighborhood in C^n of p0 . When do C-R functions on M ∩ U extend to {r > 0}?
target_in_paper: Section 3, "Envelopes of holomorphy of domains in C^n," subsection 3.1 "C-R functions," Problem 3.1.1.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact formulation. It has the same local setting: a smooth real hypersurface M in C^n, a defining function r, a point p0 in M, a neighborhood U of p0, and the question of when C-R functions on M ∩ U extend to the side {r > 0}.
missing_details: It should make explicit that r is a smooth real-valued local defining function on U, meaning M ∩ U = {z in U : r(z) = 0} and dr is nonzero on M ∩ U.
The extension region should be written locally as U ∩ {r > 0}, not as an implicit global set {r > 0}.
The word "extend" should be made explicit as holomorphic extension to the positive side of the hypersurface.
The intended quantifier should be stated: the question is asking for conditions under which every C-R function on M ∩ U extends.
The scope is local at the germ of M at p0; this should be made explicit so the question is not read as a global extension problem.

The paper leaves the precise regularity class of the C-R functions implicit, so a stand-alone formulation should at least signal that the standard local hypersurface notion of C-R function is intended.
refined_question: Let M ⊂ C^n be a smooth real hypersurface, let p0 ∈ M, and let r be a smooth real-valued defining function on a neighborhood U of p0 such that M ∩ U = {z ∈ U : r(z) = 0} and dr ≠ 0 on M ∩ U. Determine the local conditions on the germ of M at p0 under which every C-R function on M ∩ U admits a holomorphic extension to the one-sided neighborhood U ∩ {z ∈ U : r(z) > 0}.
justification: The draft is targeting exactly Problem 3.1.1. The paper states the problem tersely, in problem-list style, under the heading "Envelopes of holomorphy of domains in C^n" and subsection "C-R functions." A faithful refinement therefore should not broaden the problem, but only unpack the standard implicit meanings: that r is a local defining function, that the relevant side is the local side U ∩ {r > 0}, that the extension sought is holomorphic, and that the question concerns local one-sided extendability for C-R functions near p0.
